title: Romanticism & the Sublime
description: Nature at its most awe-inspiring, and the human drama set against it.

items.title: In the Sea
items.medium: Oil on panel
items.description_narrative: Arnold Böcklin's "In the Sea" is an oil on panel painting created in 1883, depicting a dramatic marine scene. The work exemplifies Böcklin's imaginative approach to mythological subjects within a vivid seascape.
items.tags: symbolism, mythological, marine, 19th century, fantasy, painting, european

items.title: Distant View of Niagara Falls
items.medium: Oil on wood panel
items.description_narrative: Thomas Cole's Distant View of Niagara Falls, painted in 1830 with oil on wood panel, presents a sweeping vista of the iconic natural wonder. This work exemplifies Cole's profound engagement with the American landscape, often imbued with a sense of the sublime and picturesque.
items.tags: landscape, American art, romanticism, sublime, nature, Niagara Falls, oil painting

items.title: New England Scenery
items.cultural_context: Hudson River School, American Romanticism, 19th Century American
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Thomas Cole's 'New England Scenery' captures the wild grandeur of the American landscape. This 1839 oil on canvas work exemplifies the romantic vision of nature central to Cole's artistic output.
items.tags: landscape, american art, hudson river school, romanticism, 19th century, nature, sublime

items.title: The Good Shepherd
items.medium: Lithograph on white wove plate paper
items.description_narrative: This lithograph by Thomas Cole, titled "The Good Shepherd" and created in 1849, likely portrays a traditional religious theme. The work, rendered on white wove plate paper, evokes a sense of spiritual guidance within a serene landscape.
items.tags: religious, pastoral, romanticism, allegorical, 19th century, american art, lithography

items.title: Portrait of John D. Rockefeller
items.medium: Wood engraving on cream China paper, tipped onto ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This wood engraving by Timothy Cole depicts a portrait of the prominent American industrialist John D. Rockefeller. Created in 1921, the work demonstrates Cole's masterful technique in printmaking, capturing the subject with intricate detail.
items.tags: portrait, john d. rockefeller, industrialist, wood engraving, printmaking, american art, 20th century

items.title: A Friendly Warning
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas, titled 'A Friendly Warning,' presents a narrative scene inviting viewer contemplation. The artist, Thomas Hicks, utilized traditional painting techniques to convey the depicted interaction.
items.tags: painting, 19th century, american art, narrative, figurative, oil painting

items.title: Capture of the Tripoli by the Enterprise
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: This historical painting by Thomas Birch depicts the dramatic naval engagement between the USS Enterprise and the Tripolitan ship Tripoli. Rendered in oil on canvas, it captures a pivotal moment from the First Barbary War.
items.tags: naval, historical, marine, early american, war, 19th century, dramatic

items.title: Pergola with Oranges
items.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: Thomas Fearnley's 'Pergola with Oranges' depicts a sun-drenched architectural structure adorned with citrus fruits. This oil painting on paper, later mounted on canvas, captures a serene moment through its vibrant depiction of light and nature.
items.tags: pergola, oranges, garden, romanticism, landscape, picturesque, vibrant

items.title: Coming Squall (Nahant Beach with a Summer Shower)
items.cultural_context: Early American Landscape Painting, American Romanticism
items.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on cradled panel
items.description_narrative: This oil painting captures the dramatic moment of a summer squall approaching Nahant Beach, showcasing the powerful forces of nature. Dark, heavy clouds loom over an agitated sea, conveying the impending weather event with striking realism.
items.tags: landscape, seascape, storm, nature, romanticism, early american, dramatic

items.title: Apollo and Marsyas
items.medium: Oil on panel
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts the mythological contest between the god Apollo and the satyr Marsyas, a narrative often explored in art to symbolize the conflict between order and chaos or divine and earthly music. The work, rendered in oil on panel, captures a moment from this dramatic ancient Greek story.
items.tags: mythology, classical, German art, painting, narrative, late 19th century, symbolist

items.title: Study for "William Rush Carving His Allegorical Figure of the Schuylkill River"
items.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on board
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas study by Thomas Eakins depicts American sculptor William Rush at work. Rush is shown meticulously carving his allegorical figure of the Schuylkill River in his Philadelphia studio.
items.tags: realism, american art, portraiture, sculpture, studio scene, 19th century, preparatory study

items.title: Summit of the Sierras
items.medium: Gouache over graphite, on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: Thomas Moran's 'Summit of the Sierras' masterfully captures the rugged grandeur of the American West using gouache over graphite. This work vividly portrays the majestic peaks of the Sierra Nevada mountains, reflecting the sublime beauty of the natural landscape.
items.tags: landscape, american west, sierra nevada, mountains, gouache, romanticism, sublime

items.title: Portrait of Mary Adeline Williams
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Thomas Eakins's 1899 oil on canvas depicts Mary Adeline Williams with a characteristic directness and psychological insight. His work is celebrated for its unvarnished realism, capturing the sitter's individual presence with a precise eye.
items.tags: portrait, realism, american art, oil painting, late 19th century, psychological, contemplative

items.title: Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Joseph Mallord William Turner’s "Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish" captures a dynamic maritime scene. The artwork showcases his distinctive use of light and atmosphere to depict the bustling activity surrounding fishing vessels.
items.tags: seascape, marine, romanticism, atmospheric, fishing, boats, 19th century

items.title: Valley of Aosta: Snowstorm, Avalanche, and Thunderstorm
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: This dramatic oil painting by J.M.W. Turner captures the overwhelming power of nature within the rugged Alpine landscape of the Aosta Valley. The scene dynamically combines a snowstorm, an avalanche, and a thunderstorm, illustrating the sublime forces at play.
items.tags: romanticism, landscape, snowstorm, avalanche, thunderstorm, sublime, dramatic, nature

items.title: View of Lucerne
items.medium: Watercolor, with scraping on white wove paper
items.description_narrative: J.M.W. Turner captures the dramatic light and atmospheric conditions over Lake Lucerne in this watercolor. Through delicate washes and precise scraping on white wove paper, he evokes the interplay of light and mist characteristic of his late work.
items.tags: lucerne, landscape, romanticism, british art, watercolor, atmospheric, sublime

items.title: Sunset and Moonrise
items.medium: Watercolor and gouache over traces of graphite, on ivory wove paper, laid down on board
items.description_narrative: Joseph Mallord William Turner masterfully captures the fleeting atmospheric effects of light as day transitions to night in this dynamic landscape, where the sun sets and the moon begins to rise. Executed in watercolor and gouache, this work showcases his innovative approach to depicting natural phenomena with vibrant color and expressive brushwork.
items.tags: landscape, romanticism, sunset, moonrise, atmosphere, watercolor, sublime, light

items.title: The Frontispiece to Liber Studiorum
items.medium: Mezzotint and etching in dark brown on cream laid paper, lined at edges with ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This frontispiece introduces Joseph Mallord William Turner's renowned 'Liber Studiorum' series, a collection of prints meant to illustrate the range of landscape art. Created using the techniques of mezzotint and etching, it demonstrates the artist's mastery in printmaking.
items.tags: landscape, printmaking, etching, mezzotint, romanticism, british art, instructional, frontispiece

items.title: Basle, plate 5 from Liber Studiorum
items.medium: Etching and engraving in brown on ivory paper
items.description_narrative: This print, titled 'Basle,' is plate 5 from J.M.W. Turner's influential series 'Liber Studiorum.' Through the combined techniques of etching and engraving in brown on ivory paper, Turner masterfully renders a dramatic landscape.
items.tags: etching, engraving, printmaking, landscape, riverscape, romanticism, british art

items.title: Aesacus and Hesperie, plate 66 from Liber Studiorum
items.medium: Etching and engraving in brown on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This etching and engraving depicts the mythological tale of Aesacus and Hesperie, showcasing the dramatic intensity characteristic of J.M.W. Turner's printmaking. It is plate 66 from Turner's ambitious series, Liber Studiorum, a collection of landscape studies exploring various compositional and atmospheric effects.
items.tags: mythology, classical, landscape, romanticism, printmaking, etching, engraving, british art
